### Shape

#### Description

It runs the full height of the window beneath the ribbon, to the left of the body and the chat input along its bottom, the only sidebar on the body's left. It is two parts side by side: the view bar, a narrow strip of icons down its left edge, and beside it the view picked, which holds that view's panels. Only one view shows at a time. The sidebar's thin line, its resize handle, is down the right edge of the view, where it meets the body.

#### View Bar

The view bar is 40 pixels wide, the full height of the sidebar, on the theme's darkest surface, a step darker than the views, with a thin line in the theme's line colour down its right. It holds a button per view, top to bottom, each 40 pixels square, its icon 20 pixels, centred, in the theme's muted text colour, and its tooltip the view's name with its shortcut. The view showing has its icon in the theme's text colour and a bar 2 pixels wide down the button's left edge in the theme's accent, as VS Code marks it; hovering any button shows the theme's hover behind it. The views, in order:
- Files, a folder icon, Ctrl+Shift+E (Cmd+Shift+E on macOS)
- Git, a branch icon, Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G on macOS), with a small badge on its icon counting the files changed and not yet committed, in the theme's accent, left out at none
- Run, a play-circle icon, Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS), with a small spinner on its icon while a task runs, and a dot in the theme's accent once a task has started since the view was last shown
Clicking a view's button shows that view. Clicking the button of the view already showing collapses the sidebar to the view bar alone, leaving the body the rest of the width, and clicking any button then expands it again, showing that view at the width it had. Each view's shortcut does the same as clicking its button. The bar is always there, collapsed or not, and never scrolls; its buttons never take keyboard focus away from the chat input but when pressed.

#### Views

Each view fills the sidebar beside the bar, its panels one above the other as a sidebar holds them, each headed as every sidebar panel is, with the view's name as the first panel's title:
- Files: the FileTreeScope alone, filling the view
- Git: the GitPanelScope alone, filling the view, its changes list taking the height the git panel's own sections leave, no longer squeezed beneath the file tree
- Run: the running task's ReferencedFilesPanel, UnderstandingPanel, and SubagentsPanel, one above the other, sized and resized as the Run view says, of the task selected in the MessageList
While no task runs and none has run since the project was opened, the Run view shows a single muted line, "No task running", centred. Once a task has run, it keeps showing the last task's referenced files, understanding, and subagents until the next starts, its panel headings saying the task they are for is over, muted.
The Git panel and the file tree no longer share a view: the edge that was dragged between them is gone, and each view has the whole height. Everything else about each panel stays as its own spec says.

#### Following

Files shows to start with. While a task runs, the sidebar doesn't switch views on its own: the Run button's spinner and dot say something is happening, and the user picks it. The view showing, whether the sidebar is collapsed, and its width are kept while the application runs, the same for every project, and the views keep their own scroll and selection when another is shown.

#### Run View

The Run view's panels sit one above the other: the referenced files at the top, the understanding beneath them, and the subagents and background commands last, along the bottom, beneath both. The referenced files are only as tall as their rows need, up to half the view's height, scrolling beyond that; the subagents and commands, once there are any, are only as tall as their rows need, up to 30% of the view's height; and the understanding fills what is left between them, until they are resized. While the run has started no subagent or background command, the understanding reaches the view's bottom.
The panels themselves can be resized, as the sidebar can. The edge between one panel and the next, where the lower panel's header meets the body of the one above, is a handle: dragging it up or down moves that edge, the panel above growing as the one below shrinks, or the other way, their contents laid out anew at each height as it changes. Hovering the handle shows the resize cursor for up and down and a thin line along the edge in the theme's accent, which goes once the pointer leaves and the drag is over; otherwise no line is drawn there, the change of colour still being the edge.
No panel can be dragged shorter than its header and one row of its contents, 32 pixels below its header, nor can one be pushed out of the sidebar. Once a panel has been dragged, it keeps its height rather than being only as tall as its rows need: the referenced files no longer fit their rows or stop at half the view, and scroll once their rows are taller than the height they were given. The heights they were dragged to are kept while the application runs, the next time the Run view is shown again included, as its width is; when the view's height changes, as when the window is resized, the referenced files and the subagents keep their heights and the understanding takes what is left, as far as the smallest heights allow. Double-clicking the handle puts both panels back as they start, the referenced files fitting their rows again.
Neither panel has a permanent scrollbar, since its column would break the 8 pixel inset: a panel shows its scrollbar only while its contents are taller than it, and none otherwise. When it shows, it is the same scrollbar as every other, as the [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) says.
A panel whose contents fit doesn't scroll at all, not even by a pixel, at any display scale or window size: it counts as taller than its contents need only once they overflow it by a whole pixel or more, so what is left over from rounding to the display's pixels never counts, and while they fit, it stays scrolled to its top. So neither the wheel nor a drag moves rows that all fit, and no scrollbar shows for them.

It pushes rather than covers: from the first frame of the slide to the last, the body's tab bar, the message list or open file beneath it, and the chat input end exactly at the sidebar's left edge, narrowing as it grows and widening as it shrinks, laid out again each frame, as the [BodyScope](../../../scope/application/Body.md#body-scope) says. Nothing runs beneath the sliding sidebar, nothing is clipped by it, and nothing jumps to a new width once the slide settles.

content.text:
The Run panels now live in a new VS Code-style left sidebar, and the right sidebar holds only the Tasks list. The build is clean and a new test checks switching views and collapsing. Everything else passes except one unrelated window-restart test, which failed in the full run as it has in earlier runs.

**Left sidebar** (`src/main_window.rs`):
- **View bar:** a 40px icon strip on the darkest surface with three views:
  - Files (Ctrl+Shift+E)
  - Git (Ctrl+Shift+G), with a badge counting uncommitted files
  - Run (Ctrl+Shift+R), with a spinner while a task runs and an accent dot once a task has started since you last looked
  - On macOS the shortcuts use Cmd.
- **Selected view:** shown in full-strength colour with a 2px accent bar down the left of its button.
- **Collapsing:** clicking the view already showing collapses the sidebar to just the bar, and any button opens it again.
- **Views:**
  - Files and Git each take the full height, and the draggable edge between them is gone. Outside a git repository the Git view says "Not a Git repository".
  - Run shows the referenced files, understanding and subagents panels, resizable as before.
  - Run says "No task running" until a task has run. After a task ends it keeps showing it, with a muted line saying that task is over.
- **No automatic switching:** Files shows first, and the sidebar never switches views by itself.

**Right sidebar:** its Run/Tasks tab row is gone, and it no longer switches to Run when a task starts. It still slides out while a task runs or something is queued.

**Tests:** four tests that check the Run panels themselves now show them in the right sidebar through a test-only switch, since only the full window draws the left sidebar. Three tests about the tree and Git panel sharing one column were removed, as that layout is gone.

The spec asks for a "task is over" note in the panel headings; I put a single muted line above the panels instead. Ctrl+Shift+R may clash with other shortcuts on your setup.
